Hi Carla — great talking yesterday. I put together three reservation options below tailored to your traffic profile and latency targets. I attached a one‑page proposal and a cost model CSV for line‑iteming.

TL;DR — three paths depending on risk tolerance and unit‑cost goals:

1) Pilot / Canary (Low commitment) — Short ramp, predictable testing
- Minimum committed: 8 A100(80GB) equiv GPUs (spot/reserved mix)
- Expected usable throughput: ~80–120 qps for short sequences (with batching)
- Ramp: 2 weeks pilot -> expand to 16 in month 1 if PoC passes
- Burst: automated burst to Dedicated pool up to 32 GPUs for 4 hours/day
- Cost: lowest upfront, higher per‑unit token cost
- Notes: Good for model validation and latency testing; preserves ability to move quickly.

2) Growth runway (Balanced) — Moderate commitment, predictable unit economics
- Minimum committed: 32 A100(80GB) equiv GPUs (reserved)
- Expected steady throughput: ~400–600 qps depending on model family and quantization
- Ramp: pilot (2 weeks) -> production baseline (30 days) -> scale to target usage over 90 days
- Burst: 50% burst capacity available (up to +16 GPUs) with warmup credits for prefix caching
- Cost: better per‑token than Pilot; recommended quantization: 4bit/8bit mixed depending on evals
- SLA: 99.9% uptime with 30‑minute remediation playbook

3) Anchored Commitment (High commitment, best unit cost)
- Minimum committed: 96 A100(80GB) equiv GPUs with reserved lanes and cross‑region failover
- Throughput: supports full scale plus sustained background batch jobs (embeddings + rerank)
- Ramp: 30–60 day staged activation with phased decommits and a 3‑month smoothing window to manage burn rate
- Burst: up to 2x burst capacity for scheduled peak windows; dedicated prewarm pool included
- Cost: lowest per‑token; includes SLA (99.95%) + incident review cadence and custom runbook

Engineering recommendations (brief):
- Quantization: start with BF16/8bit for safety and move to 4bit for reranking workloads after evals
- Cache strategy: aggressive prefix and KV caching for common prompts to reduce GPU cycles
- Canary plan: 2‑node canary on same region with traffic steering and automatic rollback

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick internal alignment call (30m) to pick the path (Pilot | Growth | Anchored)
2) We’ll provide a formal SOW and sample PoC schedule within 48 hours once you pick a path
3) If you want procurement language up front, we can include a PO checklist and DocuSign template in the SOW

Attachments: Opsynapse_Reservation_Proposal_0427.pdf, gpu_cost_model_opsynapse_0427.csv

Thanks — I can jump on a call tomorrow afternoon or Wed morning.

— Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts
